$description: The design-token source for the mjx-ooxml-rs client platform (MJXOFF-156). The `color`, `font`, `font-weight`, `text`, `leading`, `tracking`, `radius`, `spacing`, `shadow`, `ease` and `duration` groups are the allr.work values as measured in docs/client-platform/DESIGN_TOKENS.md §1 — read from the site's own stylesheet, never approximated. The `theme` and `document` groups are this project's three additions (§2.1, §2.2, §2.3): a derived dark palette, a document-surface palette that keeps the page true white in both schemes, and the contrast metadata that turns §2.2's rule into a build failure. This file is the ONLY hand-edited artefact in the pipeline; ui/tokens/tokens.css, ui/tokens/tokens.ts and crates/mjx-tokens/src/generated.rs are emitted from it by `cargo run -p xtask -- tokens`. FORMAT: W3C Design Tokens Community Group format, in its string profile — `color` is `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`, `dimension` is a CSS length such as `8px`, `duration` is `150ms`. The later drafts' object forms carry no information this pipeline uses and would make the one hand-edited file in the pipeline three times longer. EXTENSIONS live under the `mjx` key: `rustType` names the struct a group becomes in Rust; `schemes` marks a group whose children are colour schemes; `usage` and `background` are the contrast metadata, required on every colour token.

color.$description: The allr.work palette, verbatim. Warm and organic: the neutrals are beige rather than grey and the `black` is a green. These are the names the site itself declares, so dropping the platform into a host that already defines them re-themes it with no code change.

white.$description: true white; the site declares it beside `card` and this file keeps both names.

ink.$description: primary text — a deep, desaturated green-black.

green.$description: primary accent. DESIGN_TOKENS.md §2.2: 3.39 : 1 on white — legal for UI components and large text, ILLEGAL for body text. Fills, borders, indicators and icons only; `green-deep` is the accent-coloured text colour.

green-deep.$description: accent, pressed / on-light text. DESIGN_TOKENS.md §2.2: 5.34 : 1 on white — legal for body text.

honey-deep.$description: secondary accent, deep. Measured at 3.49 : 1 on white by this generator, so — unlike `green-deep`, its counterpart in the green ramp — it is NOT legal for body text and is tagged `fill-only`. DESIGN_TOKENS.md §2.2 measured only the greens; this is the honey ramp's answer to the same question.

font.$description: The site's three families. Young Serif is display-only — empty states and onboarding, never the chrome and never document content.

sans.$description: the chrome face; a rounded humanist that reads slightly wider than a typical UI font.

mono.$description: DESIGN_TOKENS.md §1 elides this stack after `Liberation Mono`; the elision is the standard Tailwind v4 monospace stack, written out here in full.

font-weight.$description: The four weights the site loads. DESIGN_TOKENS.md §1 records the values but not the custom-property names; these are Tailwind v4's own (`--font-weight-*`), which is the layer the site's theme is written in.

text.$description: The two small type sizes the site declares. Dense editor surfaces — the formula bar, the cell grid, a properties inspector — use `xs` with `leading.tight`, not the site's relaxed body measure.

body.$description: DESIGN_TOKENS.md §1 records this as `body line-height` with no custom-property name of its own; it joins the `leading` family here.

radius.$description: The radii are large, and that is the most recognisable part of the source's character. Toolbars and inspectors keep that softness rather than reverting to the 2–4px corners Office uses.

spacing.$description: The base spacing step, from which the site's spacing scale is multiplied. It is a token in its own right rather than a group so that its custom property is `--spacing`, exactly as the site declares it.

shadow.$description: Shadows are ink-tinted, never neutral black.

lift.$description: the site's one elevation, tinted with `color.ink` at 11% alpha.

ease.$description: `spring` overshoots: right for a panel or sheet entering, wrong for anything attached to a document object, where overshoot reads as imprecision. Selection, handles and canvas motion use `ink`.

duration.$description: DESIGN_TOKENS.md §1 records the site's `default duration` of 0.15s with no custom-property name of its own; it is named `--duration-transition` here for what it is.

theme.$description: The semantic application palette, in both colour schemes. DESIGN_TOKENS.md §2.1: the source stylesheet has no `prefers-color-scheme` block, no `.dark` class and no `[data-theme]` selector, so the dark scheme is DERIVED — the source's hue relationships held and lightness inverted, so the dark theme reads as the same brand rather than a different product. The two schemes must carry exactly the same member names; the generator fails if they drift, because a semantic role that exists in one scheme and not the other is a component that cannot be themed.

accent.$description: fills, borders, indicators and icons. NOT text — see `accent-pressed`.

accent-pressed.$description: the pressed accent, and the only accent-coloured text colour on a light surface.

accent.$description: kept `fill-only` for symmetry with the light scheme, where the same role fails body-text contrast. A component that may not colour text with the accent in one scheme may not do it in the other either.

accent-pressed.$description: the light scheme's accent becomes the dark scheme's pressed accent, and is the accent-coloured text colour on a dark surface.

document.$description: The document-surface palette. DESIGN_TOKENS.md §2.3: an editor has TWO palettes and conflating them is the classic mistake. The page stays true white in both schemes — a document is white paper, and a warm-tinted or dark page changes what the author sees relative to what they will print or send. What changes with the scheme is the canvas backdrop behind the page, the page shadow, and the in-canvas UI. A reading-mode inversion of the page itself is a user setting, not a theme consequence. These are the tokens the Rust canvas needs and a CSS custom property cannot reach it, which is the reason this pipeline emits three artefacts instead of one.

backdrop.$description: `color.paper` behind a true-white page makes the page read as a distinct, lit object rather than dissolving into the background.

tracked-change-insert.$description: tagged `fill-only`: measured against the page it does not reach 4.5 : 1, so it is legal for the change bar, the underline rule and the marker, and a tracked insertion's own glyphs must stay `theme.*.text-primary`.

tracked-change-delete.$description: tagged `fill-only` for the same reason as `tracked-change-insert`.

page.$description: true white in the dark scheme too — §2.3's whole point.

tracked-change-insert.$description: the page stays white in the dark scheme, so this is measured against white like its light-scheme counterpart.
